tasks.title: P30-01 — D101: the restored control cluster mounts, acts, and tells the truth (Q118 = RESTORE)
tasks.description: Restore the zoom/magnifier/Reset cluster in the live page (Q118 = RESTORE, final) so it mounts, acts and never advertises a refused state. `chart.html` gains a `#controls` toolbar, `chart.js::init` mounts it once per page load through `mountControlCluster()`, and a click applies the page's own `zoom(range, factor)` / `fitAndFollow()` locally then reports one `{"control", "value"}` on `LwBridge.controlPressed` and returns nothing; Python validates the id, calls the unchanged `handle_control`, and only the durable `router_mode` op returns (no page consumer is added for the published `zoom`/`reset_view` — a replayed log replays state, never steps). `mountControls` becomes idempotent per container and applies the three-branch latch rule, `ui/chart_controls.CONTROL_SPECS` becomes the one declaration `ui/lwc_view.CONTROL_IDS` derives from, and the new exported `syncControlState(op)` drives the magnifier's `aria-pressed` from the mode op. Four offscreen layers prove reachability (a DOM suite, a real-page-glue suite, the pytest bridge path, a four-way join); the painted page is owner-run G7 and no case, exit condition or record may claim it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the page loaded, Then a control container exists, `mountControls` has run exactly once per page load (and once after a render-process recovery), and each control id from the mirror is present in the DOM and activates the corresponding router action. (Measurable: DOM presence per id + an action assertion per control against the existing router seam; a page-recovery case asserting exactly one mount.)

Given a toggle control whose action is refused (TR-9), Then after the handler returns `aria-pressed` describes the app's actual state — it equals its pre-click value (revert) or the mode the router returned (drive-from-return), and in **neither** case does it read `true` for a refused state — and the refusal is reported exactly once. The refused path is tested from **both** starting states (off→refused, on→refused). (Measurable: attribute read before/after each refused click in both states + a report counter; a click-handler unit case driving `mountControls` with a refusing `onControl`.)

Given the end state, Then every control id in the mirror is reachable in the running page, and **no** control surface exists whose only callers are tests — the reachability check joins the mirror's ids to the DOM, so a surface that regresses to test-only fails it. (Measurable: the join of mirror ids → DOM ids → the action each performs; a negative case where an id is removed from the DOM and the check goes red.)

Given the restored cluster, When the user pans and zooms from the keyboard, Then the documented page affordances still work unchanged alongside the buttons. (Measurable: the existing keyboard/interaction tests, unmodified.)

Given the restored cluster, When a control is clicked in the page, Then its message reaches `LwcChartView.handle_control` through the bridge (the production caller that did not exist), the corresponding Python action runs, and no Python-side control surface remains referenced only by tests or by the mirror — `ChartControls` is either the receiving surface or its signal names are carried by a module production imports. (Measurable: an offscreen end-to-end click per control asserting the Python slot ran; a production-reference check for `handle_control` and `ChartControls` that fails on a test-only symbol.)

Given the working tree after this task, Then the only paths this task created or modified are `chart_assets/lwc/chart.html`, `chart_assets/lwc/interaction.js`, `chart_assets/lwc/chart.js`, `chart_assets/lwc/interaction.controls.test.js`, `chart_assets/lwc/controls.test.js`, `ui/chart_controls.py`, `ui/lwc_bridge.py`, `ui/lwc_view.py` and `tests/test_d101_control_cluster.py`; every named existing suite and `chart_assets/lwc/chart.test.js` is byte-identical to baseline `956f9f8` (`git diff --quiet 956f9f8 -- <paths>` exits 0); no case in either new suite mentions `QWebEngineView`, `grab(` or a screenshot (G7 stays owner-run and unclaimed); and no case invents a data-limit refusal — the only refusal driven is TR-9 (`enter_zoom` from `ALARM_PLACING`), while the no-visible-range press asserts no viewport change, no `zoomRefused`, one report (`FI-P30-1`).

tests.description: `chart_assets/lwc/interaction.controls.test.js` cases (a) and (b): the file builds its own stub `globalThis.document` (`createElement` returning a button fake with `setAttribute`/`getAttribute`/`appendChild`/`addEventListener`/`click`, plus `getElementById`), a stub container and a recording `onControl`; mount once, then mount again into the same container.
tests.expected_result: Four buttons with ids `control-zoom-out`, `control-zoom-in`, `control-magnifier`, `control-reset`, appended in `CONTROL_BUTTONS` order, the magnifier alone carrying `aria-pressed="false"`; the second call returns the same four buttons and appends nothing (`container.children.length === 4`). Run on the pre-fix `mountControls` this file appends four each call, so the idempotence half is red before the fix.

tests.description: `chart_assets/lwc/controls.test.js` cases (a)–(c): `globalThis.document` is a per-id element map (`chart` with `clientWidth`/`clientHeight`, `goToLatest`, `controls` recording children, everything else `null`) with `createElement`/`getElementById` and `readyState = "complete"`; `LightweightCharts` is a fake tree sized to `init()`; `window.LwInteraction` is the real `require("./interaction.js")`; `window.lwBridge` is a recorder. Load the real page glue, click `control-zoom-in`, then click `control-reset` after an arrow-key pan.
tests.expected_result: (a) after load `controls.children.length === 4` with ids `control-zoom-out` … `control-reset` in mirror order, `#chart`'s `clientWidth`/`clientHeight` equal the document's at a 400 px width, and the container's box stays inside the right price-scale gutter; (b) the zoom-in click calls the recorder exactly once with `{"control": "zoom-in", "value": null}` and narrows the fake visible range exactly once about its midpoint by 0.8, with no second range change in the same turn; (c) the reset click re-frames the series and `page.lwIsFollowing()` is `true`.

tests.description: `controls.test.js` case (g) — the FI-P30-1 case: `timeScale().getVisibleLogicalRange()` returns `null` (a page with no bars); click `control-zoom-in`.
tests.expected_result: The fake range is still `null` (no viewport change) and the recorder bridge receives **no** `zoomRefused`, while the press is still reported exactly once with `{"control": "zoom-in", "value": null}` — the report is unconditional and only the viewport change is guarded by `if (range)`. No data-limit refusal is asserted anywhere.

tests.description: `interaction.controls.test.js` cases (c) off→refused, (d) on→refused, (e) accepted, (f) no synchronous answer: each clicks the stub button with a recording `onControl`; (d) pre-sets `aria-pressed="true"` before the click (AP-P30-3 — the router cannot be `ZOOMING` and `ALARM_PLACING` at once, so the second starting state is constructed).
tests.expected_result: Off→refused (pre-click `"false"`, request `true`, result `{refused: true, mode: "ALARM_PLACING"}`): the attribute is `"false"` — its pre-click value, never the refused request — and the recorder bridge saw exactly one `zoomRefused`. On→refused (pre-click `"true"`, request `false`, same refusal): the attribute is **not** `"false"` (it never adopts the refused request) and exactly one `zoomRefused` fires. Accepted: `{mode: "ZOOMING"}` → `"true"`, then `{mode: "IDLE"}` → `"false"`, no report. No synchronous answer (`onControl` returns `undefined`): the attribute is unchanged and no `zoomRefused` fires. The invariant asserted in both refusal directions is 'the attribute never equals the state the refused click requested'; the pre-fix handler writes the request before the call, so both refusal cases are red before the fix.

tests.description: `controls.test.js` cases (d)/(e): drive `page.lwApplyChannel("interaction", {v: 1, ops: [...]})` through the real dispatcher with `{op: "router_mode", mode: "ZOOMING"}`, then `{op: "reset_view", mode: "IDLE"}`, then `{op: "zoom", step: 1}`, then a `router_mode` op carrying `refused: true, mode: "ALARM_PLACING"`, then replay the first mode op.
tests.expected_result: `#control-magnifier`'s `aria-pressed` becomes `"true"` for the ZOOMING mode and `"false"` for the IDLE `reset_view`; the bare `zoom` op makes `syncControlState` return `false` and changes nothing; the refused `router_mode` op leaves the attribute `"false"` — never the refused state; replaying the mode op changes nothing further.

tests.description: `tests/test_d101_control_cluster.py` join cases: a stdin node script defines `globalThis.document` (the same stub shape) **before** requiring `interaction.js`, reads `CONTROL_BUTTONS` and mounts them into a stub container (the `tests/test_lwc_router_mirror.py` `_NODE` + stdin-script pattern); an in-module `missing_ids(...)` helper then compares the mounted ids to `LV.CONTROL_IDS` and `[s.id for s in CONTROL_SPECS]` and each row's `intent`/`toggle`/`signal`; the negative case deletes one mounted button from the stub first.

class ControlSpec(NamedTuple):
    """One in-page control: its DOM id, ChartControls' signal, the page's intent."""
    id: str
    signal: str
    intent: str
    toggle: bool

CONTROL_SPECS = (
    ControlSpec("zoom-out", "zoom_out", "zoom_out", False),
    ControlSpec("zoom-in", "zoom_in", "zoom_in", False),
    ControlSpec("magnifier", "magnify_toggled", "magnify_toggle", True),
    ControlSpec("reset", "reset", "reset", False),
)  # the ONE declaration; module docstring gains the sentence naming it the single source

from ui.chart_controls import CONTROL_SPECS
CONTROL_IDS = tuple(spec.id for spec in CONTROL_SPECS)  # same four ids, same order; the hand-kept literal is DELETED

tasks.title: P30-02 — D102 + D103: a popup dismissed by its owner, a selection restored by identity
tasks.description: Collapsing the watchlist dismisses its floating search-results popup, and a drawing-group checkbox toggle no longer wipes the drawing selection. `_apply_collapsed_visual` calls `clear_search_results()` on collapse (so every collapse path is covered: the header toggle, the collapsed bar, `toggle_collapsed`, `set_collapsed`), `show_search_results` clears and returns while collapsed so an in-flight result cannot resurrect the popup, and `DrawingGroupsDialog.reload` captures the selected drawing ids before rebuilding and re-selects the surviving ids by `UserRole` id — never by row index. The new suite proves the popup case can fail before it proves it passes (AR-P30-11) and asserts the restored selection is the set of surviving ids.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given visible search results, When the watchlist collapses, Then the popup is hidden and its items are cleared. (Measurable: `isVisible()` false + list count zero.)
Given a query in flight, When the panel collapses and the results arrive afterwards, Then the popup does not become visible. (Measurable: collapse → deliver results → visibility assertion.)

Given two selected drawings, When a group's `visible` (or `locked`) checkbox is toggled, Then the same drawing ids remain selected and the subsequent action receives them. (Measurable: selected-id list before/after + the action's received ids.)

Given a reload that reorders or shrinks the list, Then the restored selection contains exactly the surviving ids and nothing else. (Measurable: a fixture where a drawing is removed between selection and restore.)

Given the working tree after this task, Then the only paths created or modified are `ui/watchlist_panel.py`, `ui/drawing_groups_dialog.py` and `tests/test_d102_d103_surface_state.py`; `tests/test_d39_burst_search.py`, `tests/test_watchlist_collapsed_bar_d44.py`, `tests/test_dock_widths_collapsed_d44.py`, `tests/test_p9_group_dialog.py`, `tests/test_p9_group_payload.py`, `tests/test_p9_active_group.py`, `tests/test_p10_groups_dialog_lock.py` and `tests/test_drawing_store.py` are byte-identical to baseline `956f9f8` and green; no cancellation, debounce, service, settings key, extra widget or persistence change is made.

tests.description: `tests/test_d102_d103_surface_state.py::TestWatchlistPopupDismissal` case (a), parametrized over the three collapse entry points (`set_collapsed(True)`, `_on_header_toggled(False)`, `toggle_collapsed()`): a `WatchlistPanel` built offscreen, `show_search_results([_desc(...), ...])`, then the collapse.
tests.expected_result: For each entry point the popup is hidden (`panel._search_popup.isHidden() is True`, and `isVisible() is False` where the offscreen platform reports visibility for a `Qt.Popup`) and `panel._search_list.count() == 0`. The case is first run against the un-fixed handler with the survivor recorded in the result (AR-P30-11); if the platform reports the popup as not-visible even when shown, the assertion falls back to `isHidden()` plus the list count, which distinguishes the two states regardless.

tests.description: Case (b): collapse (with results visible), then expand again.
tests.expected_result: After re-expansion the popup is still hidden and its list still empty — expanding does not resurrect a dismissed result.

tests.description: Case (c): a query is in flight (a pending result delivery is modelled by calling `show_search_results([...])` after the collapse), then a *new* query while expanded calls `show_search_results([...])` again.
tests.expected_result: The post-collapse delivery leaves the popup hidden and the list empty (no resurrection); the later query while expanded shows the popup and populates the list — the guard is a display decision, not a permanent mute, and the service/debounce are never touched.

tests.description: `TestDrawingSelectionRestore` case (e), on the shared temp DB from `conftest.py`: one group and three drawings, two selected in `drawings_list`; toggle the group's `visible` checkbox through `_on_group_item_changed(visible_item)`; then invoke the Assign action with `DrawingStore.assign_groups` monkeypatched to record its arguments.
tests.expected_result: `_selected_drawing_ids()` before and after the toggle are identical ids in the same order, and the recorded `assign_groups` call receives exactly those two ids. On the un-fixed `reload()` the same sequence yields an empty selection, so the case is red before the fix.

tests.description: Case (f)/(i): the same toggle driven through the `locked` column, and a separate run that selects group row 0 before a toggle.
tests.expected_result: The `locked` toggle preserves the drawing ids exactly as `visible` does; selecting a group row before the toggle leaves the drawings selection unchanged — the groups table's own row selection is a different table and is deliberately not restored.

tests.description: Cases (g)/(h): (g) two drawings selected, one of them deleted from the store between selection and `reload()`, then reload; (h) a fixture where `drawings_for_symbol` returns the rows in the opposite order, then reload.
tests.expected_result: (g) the restored selection is exactly the surviving id and nothing else (the vanished id is skipped, not re-selected by position); (h) the restored ids are the same *set* as before the reorder — identity, not index — and `drawings_list` order follows the fixture without changing the selection set.

tasks.description: Make the docstrings describe the shipped engine and make `release_resources` clear what its docstring promises. Seven wording sites are 'words wrong, code right' — `ui/main_window._eastern_offset` and `build_main_chart_view`, `ui/popout_window`'s module docstring, `BAR_BYTES`, `popout_view` and `view_memory_estimate`, plus `services/chart_model.heikin_ashi`'s 'keeps its identical local copy until P6-13' — and each is rewritten (or, for `services/chart_model.py:273`, replaced by a past-tense sentence) with no code change; the dead re-host branch stays. `LwcChartView.release_resources` is the reverse — **the docstring is the contract** — so it clears `bridge._channel_logs` per channel and `bridge._channel_queue`, keeps its promise list and names the `memory_bytes` residual (AR-P30-6); `memory_bytes` itself is untouched.
